newsitem.title: USA: Wachovia to acquire Central Fidelity Banks.
newsitem.headline: Wachovia to acquire Central Fidelity Banks.

text.p: Wachovia Corp. agreed on Tuesday to buy Central Fidelity Banks Inc. for about $2.3 billion in stock, marking the North Carolina bank's second big acquisition in just two weeks.

The deal, combined with the recent agreement to buy Jefferson Bankshares Inc., will make Wachovia the largest bank in Virgina and the 17th-largest bank in the United States, up from its previous position as No. 20.
Prior to these transactions, Wachovia operated primarily in North Carolina, South Carolina and Georgia.
The company has largely stayed out of the merger frenzy gripping the banking industry. Before the Jefferson deal, its last sizable acquisition was in 1991, when it bought South Carolina National.

"Central Fidelity has an impressive franchise throughout Virginia. The company's culture is quite similar to Wachovia's, with a focus on meeting customer needs and a relationship-management approach to the market," said Wachovia Chief Executive Bud Baker.

Under the latest deal, Wachovia will swap 0.63 of a common share for each Central Fidelity common share. Based on Wachovia's closing stock price Monday of $62.625, the deal is worth about $2.3 billion, Wachovia said.
Central Fidelity's stock jumped $5.75 to $37.625 on Nasdaq, while Wachovia lost 93.75 cents to $61.6875 on the New York Stock Exchange.

As part of the agreement, Central Fidelity has granted Wachovia a stock option for about 19.9 percent of Central Fidelity's outstanding shares. The two companies also said they have each ended their stock repurchase programmes.

In a telephone conference call, Wachovia Chief Financial Officer Robert McCoy said the transaction is expected to dilute Wachovia's earnings by 13.5 percent in 1997 and between 4.0 and 4.5 percent in 1998. By 1999, it should add about 4 percent to Wachovia's earnings.

He also said Wachovia is expected to take a charge of $136 million in 1997 related to the Central Fidelity acquisition and its recently announced $540 million deal to buy Jefferson Bankshares. In 1998, the company plans to take a $54 million charge related to the Central Fidelity deal, he said.
The agreement with Central Fidelity is expected to be accounted for as a pooling of interests. Three members of the Central Fidelity board will be invited to join the Wachovia board.

Baker said the company anticipates $79 million in cost savings from the acquisition. He said the deal is likely to result in overlap in some areas, but declined to discuss estimates of potential job losses.
He also said that Wachovia still sees opportunities for growth in Virginia, especially in the northern section of the state.
"North Virginia is clearly an area where we can look for some strenghening," he said.

Although both acquisition targets are based in Virginia, experts said little overlap was expected. Wachovia has been bullish on opportunities for growth in Virginia and recently expressed interest in expanding into Maryland.
"They're picking up another very large, very good state. It's the largest bank in Virgina and it doesn't have a lot of problems," said John Mason of Interstate/Johnson Lane.
The merger has been approved by directors of both companies and is subject to approval by shareholders and regulators.
Central Fidelity, the parent of Central Fidelity National Bank in Richmond, Va., had 244 offices in Virginia and assets of $10.6 billion, making it the state's third-largest bank.
Upon completion of the Jefferson and Central Fidelity mergers, Wachovia will have assets of about $60.2 billion with about 813 offices in Virginia, the Carolinas and Georgia.
